items.note: Full Association name, 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test, not weight; station test governs (Story 1).
'Under payment by weight, nothing later would have cost any man a dollar.'
Only Teague named as bookkeeper; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill absent. The core fact, the Association's officers, is not given.
Son of Gideon correct, but manager stated as from 1911 (planted error), not 1913.
Station gain line, 5.25 percent, carried to general account, every year (Story 6).
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, tested; bottle ruled for a full charge; cream hauled to Larrow Green, skim returned. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., full invoice, $77.93.
0.19 the same in June flush and February, 'flat as a floor' (Story 4).
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Kept the station test book in his own hand for 29 seasons.
Summary leaf absent; the 1896 average of 3.80 is never given in Section A.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, question mark. Says 'markedly higher' without 3.80, but the core fact is present.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron; irony stated.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as taught, cannot say why') is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died February 1934 never cleared; test book impounded, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book 1 January 1897 preferred over 1900; scales agreeing.
Story 4 states 3.61 vs Larrow Green 3.78, then 'The deficiency was 0.19', which presents the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19. The key's gap-conflation gate applies.
The committee came up in 'Grigg's sleigh' in January and reported in March. It never states that the committee was under Grigg or that it sampled January-March 1908.
200,000 lb at 3.42 present. Proportional loss / richer herds losing more is stated only in Section C, not A.
Passed to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958.
Alder Corners, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd named, but Redlow Ridge is not ('over the ridge'). The key says the ridge gates.
Four of six Hessel Bottom farms hauled there in summer flush (1915 omitted, core fact present).
Called 'A control group'; other county (Vessey) plus the Cudd test book = two of four.
Same milk tested about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners.
Section A never states that the comparison disposes of hay and watering together (only in F).
Rosalie, daughter, ran factory after 1941, copied figures for Ivy 1958.
Strawn named but circuit dated 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23 planted error).
Lactometer on every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned whole lot.
Wrote only the condemnation, drew no inference about the years before.
Replacement dates present, but the 1924 average is given as 3.85 (planted error); 3.80 is required.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to state office 1936 and Farland 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in weigh room. Frick unnamed ('Ashlin attorney'); core fact present.
Three explanations (water/Vose, theft, bog hay); board found no cause established.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook, which nobody set beside the others.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May $3,800 'without admission', no cause established, charged to station account.
One-fifth of $19,000; charged to station account, in effect paid out of the station gain.
Ivy b.1931, granddaughter, Farland, Vaught.
Lists what she gathered, but Section A never makes the point that the records had never been in the same room (only in G).
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine surviving.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 95 percent.
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, 3.61 vs true 3.80, 0.19 = 5 percent.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, station gain = 76,000 lb (Stories 6 and 8).
Bulletin 471 October 1958; dead 24 years, out of work 33.
Granddaughter, derived via Duncan.

Second cousins with derivation (1). Declines the full/half question but then says half siblings would make them 'half second cousins', i.e. it does change the answer. The required 'does not change the answer' element fails (0). Abstained, so no -2.
Gideon, father; significance via Article VII making the station test decide pay.
'I take Duncan's word... The sources support no kinship' adopts the family denial. That is an assertion, not a declared inability to settle (A01).
$90 with explicit statement that it uses the long-run 25c average and shown working. Meets the key's acceptance condition.
5.26 percent of credited, 5.00 percent of received; denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c.
26 years 6 weeks; 25 full years 1898-1922; part-year reason given.
1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the measuring glass, borrowed measure replacing station's own.
Herds, pasture and season, same tester, machinery.
Result given only as 'markedly higher'; no 3.80 / 3.61 figures.
Rules out honesty, hay, water; limits: size of error, which piece.
Ledger (Kyle), 1911 (Falke/Orra/Duncan), Alder Corners (Hazel), post-1923 (Falke).
Independence argued; ledger, 1911 and post-1923 named as standing without 1958.
'Did the bookkeeper question the ledger? No.' is an assertion on A09.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low (complaints since 1902, 1919 circular).
Only signed sheets and 1919 circular valid. Manager date given wrongly as 1911; nothing on arguing watering at the hearing or never naming the glass. Fewer than three.
'He did not know why... he blamed the patrons' is a headline verdict on A03, not an abstention.
Row 1 (1895 vs 4 May 1896), row 7 (Orra 1866 via 'eighty-two'), row 16 (1908 committee vs 1925 board); methods stated.

NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20, broken by summing the line items) and NT-18 (great-niece in Chronicle and Falke, broken by Duncan's genealogy and Falke's correction). The run explicitly finds no other pairs.
A04 declared unsettleable (works books burned 1931). A06 and A10 are declined only in Section A, not in B-G.
Junia's 'nothing before 1900' vs her 1897 invoice; Duncan's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'.
1897 crate, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95 percent, proportional, onset 1 May 1897, nothing on farms changing. Cessation figure given as 3.85 (deducted separately).
Watering (Vose) defeated by lactometer and Alder Corners.
Theft defeated by the station gain (cream arrived heavy), 1911, same tester after 1923.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, against a constant gap.
'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.' is an assertion on A07.
'What did the tester believe? That it was something in the glass.' is an assertion on A05.
Exactly 150 words.
Invoice, test book, weigh book, ledger, Strawn notebook, Alder Corners tests, 1958 measurement.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure in the summary.
5 percent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy.
